properties.natural_language: Before a validator deposit is accepted into the pending activation state, the deposit amount must be exactly 32 ETH, the validator public key must be a valid BLS12-381 point, and the withdrawal credentials must conform to the expected format.

Before processing validator activations in an epoch, the deposit transaction must have been confirmed on the execution layer and the Merkle proof verified by the consensus layer to ensure deposit authenticity.

The activation churn limit computed by get_validator_activation_churn_limit() must never exceed MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT (8 validators per epoch), regardless of the total validator set size.

After process_registry_updates executes, if the epoch activation limit has been reached, all validators beyond the first 8 must transition to STATE-VALIDATOR-QUEUED-NEXT-EPOCH and not be activated in the current epoch.
The validator set growth rate must not exceed 57,600 new validators per month (8 validators/epoch × 225 epochs/day × 30 days), enforcing linear growth post-EIP7514 activation.
The asymmetric churn configuration must maintain that validator exits can occur at unbounded rate while entries are capped, ensuring the validator set can shrink faster than it can grow.
Before accepting an eth_config RPC request, the node must validate that the request does not exceed the rate limit of 1 request per second from the same client to prevent resource exhaustion.

Before processing an eth_config request from an external RPC client, the node should verify that the request originates from a trusted interface (localhost, private network, or authenticated connection) when security policies require access restriction.

The eth_config response must return configuration values that accurately reflect the most recent block header state with no more than one block of staleness to ensure validators receive up-to-date fork configuration.
After a fork boundary is crossed, all cached configuration data must be purged and fresh configuration loaded to ensure current/next/last fields accurately reflect the new fork state.

Before trusting configuration data from a queried node for validator preparation, the validator must cross-check the configuration against multiple independent reference nodes to detect dishonest reporting.

When rate limiting is enforced on eth_config requests, the system must prevent DDoS attacks while ensuring legitimate validator operators can query configuration at reasonable intervals (at least once per second).

The EVM_RECURSION_LIMIT constant (12288) must be enforced on all nested CALL, DELEGATECALL, STATICCALL, and CREATE operations to prevent stack overflow, with any call at or exceeding this depth failing immediately.

The relationship between EVM_RECURSION_LIMIT (12288) and the EIP-150 call depth limit (1024) must be maintained such that the gas-based limit is the primary enforcement mechanism while the recursion limit acts as a secondary safeguard for the Python reference implementation.
After a nested call exceeds the recursion limit, the call must fail with return value 0, and execution must resume at the calling context with the failure recorded on the stack.

At transaction execution start, the accessed_addresses set must be pre-warmed with the transaction sender address, recipient address, and all precompile addresses (0x01-0x09 plus chain-specific additions) before any opcode execution begins.

Before charging gas for a cold SLOAD operation, the system must verify that the storage slot (address, key) pair is not in the accessed_storage_keys set, and if cold, charge 2100 gas instead of 100 gas.

After a sub-call context reverts, all modifications to the accessed_addresses and accessed_storage_keys sets made during the reverted execution scope must be rolled back to their state before the call.

Contracts using fixed gas stipends (2300 gas) for sub-calls must not make cold state accesses within the sub-call, as cold SLOAD (2100 gas) and cold account access (2600 gas) both exceed the stipend and will cause call failure.

Before a CREATE or CREATE2 operation completes, the newly created contract address must be added to accessed_addresses to ensure subsequent interactions with the new contract are treated as warm accesses.

Before executing the ModExp precompile, the caller must provide calldata containing valid length fields for base_length, modulus_length, and exponent_length, followed by the actual base, exponent, and modulus values of specified lengths.

The gas cost for ModExp must be at least 500 gas regardless of input size, and must scale proportionally with multiplication complexity (based on operand sizes) and iteration count (based on exponent bit length) to prevent underpricing.
After ModExp execution completes, the result must be returned as a big integer padded to exactly modulus_length bytes, with leading zeros if the result is smaller than the modulus length.
Before charging gas for ModExp, if the calculated gas cost exceeds the available gas, the operation must fail with out-of-gas error without performing the modular exponentiation computation.

Before accepting a transaction into the mempool, the node must validate that the transaction's gasLimit field does not exceed 16,777,216 (2^24), rejecting any transaction that violates this cap regardless of the block gas limit.

Before accepting a block from a peer node, the validator must verify that every transaction within the block has a gasLimit at or below 16,777,216, rejecting the entire block if any transaction exceeds this cap.

A block may contain multiple transactions with a total cumulative gas exceeding 16,777,216, but each individual transaction's gasLimit must not exceed 16,777,216, ensuring per-transaction bounds while allowing flexible block composition.
After the gas cap enforcement rejects a malicious high-gas transaction, block validation time must remain bounded and predictable, preventing DoS attacks via computational resource exhaustion.

Large contract deployments that require more than 16,777,216 gas must be re-architected using CREATE2 factory patterns, proxy patterns, or split across multiple transactions to comply with the per-transaction gas cap.

Before dropping pre-merge history, the consensus layer must have fully implemented EIP-6110 (deposit logs in block) to eliminate dependency on execution layer historical deposit logs, ensuring validator deposit processing continues correctly.

Before returning data from alternate sources (e2store, Portal Network, EIP-7801), the node must validate that the retrieved block data matches canonical chain block hashes and that transaction/receipt roots are correctly verified.

After history expiry is activated, RPC requests for pre-merge data that cannot be retrieved from alternate sources must return appropriate error responses indicating data unavailability rather than returning stale or incorrect data.

After mainnet history expiry activation, nodes must continue to sync from the merge block forward, never attempting to sync from genesis, ensuring new nodes can join the network without requiring full historical data.

The activation timeline for history expiry must progress from devnet testing to Sepolia testnet (2025-05-01), then to mainnet only after Pectra fork activation, with sufficient coordination time (days to weeks) for ecosystem preparation.

For any storage operation (SLOAD/SSTORE), the warm/cold access status must be correctly determined from the transaction-scoped access sets, with warm accesses costing 100 gas and cold accesses costing 2100 gas (SLOAD) or higher (SSTORE).

Before executing SSTORE or TSTORE, the system must verify that the execution context is not in static mode (is_static = false), rejecting write operations in STATICCALL contexts with WriteInStaticContext error.

Before executing SSTORE, the system must verify that gas_left exceeds GAS_CALL_STIPEND (2300 gas), preventing storage writes in contexts with minimal gas stipends that cannot afford the operation cost.

After SSTORE execution completes, if the storage value transitions from non-zero to zero (storage clearing), a gas refund of GAS_STORAGE_CLEAR_REFUND must be added to the transaction refund counter, subject to the 20% total gas cap per EIP-3529.

Transient storage (TLOAD/TSTORE) must be isolated per (address, key) tuple within a transaction and cleared atomically at transaction completion, never persisting beyond the transaction boundary or leaking between contracts.

All transient storage operations (TLOAD/TSTORE) must charge a uniform GAS_WARM_ACCESS cost of 100 gas, never requiring cold access charging since transient storage exists only within the transaction scope.

All ADD and SUB operations must implement wrapping arithmetic modulo 2^256, such that overflow in addition wraps to zero and underflow in subtraction wraps to 2^256-1, without throwing exceptions or halting execution.
Before executing DIV, SDIV, MOD, or SMOD operations, if the divisor is zero, the operation must return U256(0) without performing division computation and without throwing an exception.

Before executing SDIV (signed division), if the dividend is -2^255 and the divisor is -1, the operation must return -2^255 (the minimum signed integer) to handle the overflow edge case where the mathematical result 2^255 cannot be represented in signed 256-bit arithmetic.

ADDMOD and MULMOD operations must use extended precision arithmetic (512-bit intermediate values) to compute (x + y) mod z and (x * y) mod z without overflow in the intermediate steps, returning zero if modulus z is zero.

After EXP (exponentiation) gas calculation, the total gas cost must equal GAS_EXPONENTIATION base cost plus (GAS_EXPONENTIATION_PER_BYTE × number of bytes in exponent), ensuring larger exponents incur proportionally higher costs to prevent computational DoS.

For SIGNEXTEND operation, if byte_num exceeds 31, the value must be returned unchanged; otherwise, the sign bit from the specified byte position must be propagated to all higher bytes, filling with 0x00 for positive or 0xFF for negative values.

Before processing an eth_sendTransaction request from a dapp, the transaction parameters must be validated to include required fields: from, to, gas, and gasPrice, rejecting requests with missing fields via notValid error.

Before accepting a dapp's RPC request via the invisible iframe, the request method must be validated against the whitelist of 43 allowed read-only methods, rejecting any write operations or non-whitelisted methods with notAllowed error.

Before allowing eth_sign method calls, the system must explicitly prohibit this method from being processed through the authorization flow, as arbitrary data signing creates replay attack vulnerabilities.

After user approves a transaction in the authorization popup, the account must be temporarily unlocked for exactly 3 seconds (if personal API is exposed) to allow transaction signing, then automatically re-lock to prevent unauthorized access.

The authorization popup must display accurate transaction details (sender, recipient, gas costs) to the user, and the popup's integrity must be protected by browser same-origin policy to prevent UI spoofing or parameter substitution attacks.

The authorization.html file served by the node must be authentic and unmodified, as a compromised authorization interface could bypass security checks, auto-approve malicious transactions, or exfiltrate private keys.

After user rejects a transaction or any error occurs during processing, the system must return an error response with matching request id, null result field, and error object containing appropriate type (cancel, JsonParse, noConnection, notAllowed, or notValid).

The entire authorization mechanism depends on a local Ethereum node being accessible; if no node is available at the specified RPC endpoint, all dapp interactions must fail gracefully with noConnection error rather than hanging or providing misleading feedback.

coverage_summary.coverage_notes: Generated comprehensive security properties covering all boundary edges from trust model analysis. Prioritized properties based on untrusted external entity interactions (depositors, RPC clients, attackers, dapps, users, peer nodes). Addressed key security concerns including input validation, gas economics, access control, and state consistency.
